utterances.text: If I could ask that we move to in the B/C/S version page 5, please, and the English version should be the next page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could you tell us -- could you explain the information that appears on page 5 to the Chamber, please. What have you recorded here?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: On this page, you have the key and you have a description of the incidents. When you conduct a forensic analysis, the first thing you do is you sketch the crime scene. One of the pages of the sketch contains a key where we list any evidence found at the scene. At the -- in the bottom half of the page, you have a description of the incident where an incident is accurately described.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, in the first paragraph of the incident, did you make a note as to the calibre of weapon that was used at this crime scene, the calibre of the shell?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was a 120-millimetre projectile.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: All right. And going down to the last paragraph on this page, do you make a reference to the origin -- the location of the origin of fire?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes. There is a reference to that. It says that it was established at the crime scene that the projectile had come in the direction of north-east in the area of Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And are you aware of who controlled that area at this time?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: At the time, the Mrkovici area was under the control of the Serb army.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could you describe the scene at the site of this shelling. What was going on at the time of the impact?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: The shell landed in Parmolinska Street. There was an unfinished building there. It had been not been finished by the time the war began. This was a new building under construction, and then the construction work stopped. Civilians built up a makeshift market, a small market, where they sold the supplies that could still be had in wartime circumstances just to make ends meet. When the shell landed, there were dozens, several dozens of civilians moving about this small market that I described.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I have these pages 4 to 6 of ter 1448 marked as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let that be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P233, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, if we could move to pages 7 to 21 of the same ter number, 1448, and if I could ask Mr. Registrar to scroll slowly through.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: While he is doing that, Mr. Hasanefendic, do you recognise what appears on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is a photo file that I produced in relation to this same investigation at Parmolinska 3A.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I have this marked as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P234, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If I could ask for pages 22 to 25 of the same ter number, 1448, to be displayed, please. There should be a fragment of an English translation, or there may be a complete English translation available, according to my records. The translation was completed yesterday, Your Honours, and it may simply not have been uploaded at this time. I'll undertake to provide Mr. Registrar with a translation as soon as possible and at any case before the end of today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. In the mean time the interpreters will -- Do you have wish to have any of it interpreted?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, there will be one paragraph which I will ask the witness about. But perhaps if we could go back to page 22, he could explain to the Trial Chamber what this document is.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanefendic, do you recognise or can you tell us what the document in front of you is?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: I recognize the refreshing the document, and I can tell you what it is. This is a report containing the results of an analysis of the traces of an explosion of a projectile, which landed on the 30th of June, 1995 following shelling at Parmolinska Street. So it's a report.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And earlier in your testimony, you described expert reports that were generated by people in bomb squad or ballistics expertise as part of the investigation of shelling or sniping. Is this one of those such reports?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is one of those.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And I note the translation in English is now available and should appear on the left-hand side of Your Honours's screen. If we could go to the last paragraph on page 25 of the B/C/S version, please. Sorry, could we move to page 24 then -- page 23. My apologies to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanefendic, could I just direction your attention to the full paragraph that appears in front of you. And does the first heading, if I could call it that, in this paragraph that begins with in your language, "na asnovu" [phoen], record information as to the calibre of the weapon?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was information there indicating the calibre of the weapon and the type of weapon. This is a light anti-personnel 120-millimetre shell, marked MK and 74 KB 9501, manufactured in the Krusik factory in Valjevo, Serbia. It even gives the month of production which is January 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And does the very last paragraph of this document also record the conclusion as to the origin of fire?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: The last paragraph provides a conclusion about the origin of fire. It says the direction from which the projectile flew in was established at the scene while conducting the on-site investigation. It's as being 50 degrees plus or minus 5 degrees, which corresponds to the area of Mrkovici and Bijoskot [phoen], and temporarily occupied by the aggressor.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I have that marked as the next exhibit, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P235, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Moving on then, and, Mr. Registrar, I will next be referring to a document at ter number 1209, and moving on to another unscheduled incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanefendic, could I ask you, do you recall investigating a shelling on Velesici on 18 July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I do recall the shelling at Velesici on the 18th of July 1995, the reason being that I was the one that conducted an on-site investigation there.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we have pages 2 to 6 of this ter number, please, and the translation that appears for everyone's benefit on the left-hand side of the page is the translation of the pages 2 to 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanefendic, can you tell us what this document is?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: This document is an official report produced by the crime inspector of the Security Services Centre in Sarajevo. This document is tantamount to a record describing the on-site investigation. This document is an official report about the circumstances of the on-site investigation of the shelling of the Velesici neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanefendic, how many shells fell on Velesici on this day?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: That day we conducted four on-site investigations in a succession; therefore, there were four shells in different areas within the Velesici area, the radius being up to 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: How many deaths were recorded as a result of this shelling?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Shelling left five persons dead, and several more persons were slightly or seriously injured.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you recall the relative age of those persons who were recorded as being injured?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: I do. I remember this on-site investigation as one of the most -- more difficult ones. Two of the persons were a father and son. The son must have been about 40 and the father was older. There were some middle-aged civilian there as well, and the fourth shell landed on a refugee centre. There were children were playing in front of the building, and all of them were wounded. So there were persons of -- from different age groups involved in this incident who were injured or killed..

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now on pages 3, 4, and 5 of this document, does -- is Vrace identified as the origin of fire for each shell?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes. The conclusion was established based on the evidence available, and the conclusion was that the shell had been fired from the Vrace area.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I have this marked as the next exhibit, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P236, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Hasanefendic, did you also make a report on any of these incidents in Velesici?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes. I made my forensic report in relation to all of the incidents that occurred there.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I then ask Mr. Registrar to call up pages 10 and 11 of the same ter number, 1209.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, Mr. Hasanefendic?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is my forensic report. I produced this on the spot at the site where the shell landed in Velesici at Mustafe Beknica [phoen] Street number 44.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I have that marked as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P238, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And could I move on to pages 21 to 23 of the same ter number, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanefendic, what is this document you see on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: This is an expert finding, an analysis of the evidence of an explosion when a projectile landed. This was produced by the bomb squad of the BH MUP Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Is that with respect to the incidents you have just been speaking about in Velesici?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the expert finding in relation to that projectile involved in the incident at Velesici that I spoke of a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If we go to page 23 of this document about two thirds of the way down the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If we go back to the first page of the document, it might be page 22. And, again, my apologies to everyone for my mistake in the numbering.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: About two thirds of the way down the page on this document, do you see a conclusion as to the calibre of the shell in this case?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Further down, please. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: What calibre -- sorry. What is the calibre of shell that is recorded as being used?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: 122-millimetre.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I have that marked as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P238, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now we'll move on to a scheduled incidents and that is one of 22 August 1995, scheduled shelling 22, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanefendic, did you take part in the investigation of a major shelling incident on the date that I just referred to, 22 August 1995?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was the forensic officer involved in the on-site investigation on that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I ask that the photograph at ter number 2943 appear on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanefendic, where did that shelling take place?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: The shelling took place at Zmaja od Bosne Street, the Bitas office building. The house number is probably 64. That's as long as we're talking about the 22nd of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That's correct, we are. Now that address that you've just given on Zmaja od Bosne of the Bitas building, approximately how far from your police station is that location?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: The Bitas building is about 80 to 100 metres from the location.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The street that the witness mentioned was Zmaja od Nocjia [phoen] and not Zmaja od Bosne.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanefendic, what do you recall the street address or the street on which the Bitas building was located?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: I do. This is Zmaja od Bosne, number 64. I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you take a look at the photograph that appears on the screen in front of you and tell us whether you recognise anything.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise the Bitas building; that's the first building I recognise. I carried out an on-site investigation there.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, with the marking tool that you should be used to by now, could you circle the Bitas building on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: All right. So this is the Bitas building.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. And with an arrow could you indicate the location of your police station in relation to the Bitas building?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: My police station is in a park between two residential buildings. I'll draw an arrow. You can't see the police station building in this photograph, but I will draw an arrow to indicate the general direction. It's in a park between these two residential buildings.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, there's a -- you've just indicated that the buildings in the immediate vicinity of your police station and Bitas are residential. Are you aware of what the higher buildings in behind to the north of your police station and the Bitas building were used for. What was their purpose?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: All the buildings you can see around the Bitas building are residential buildings. I will take one step at a time. The building that I marked as number 1 is a post office. It's not a residential building. It's at Novo Sarajevo post office. That's number 1 for you. Number 2 is the Catholic church at Dolac-Malta. Numbers 3, 4, and 5 are all residential buildings. To the right you can see two office buildings. There is the Socijalno building, numbering 6. And the Electroprivida building, which is number 7 now.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I have this marked as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P239, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanefendic, you seemed to have been in the very near vicinity of the incident that you described for us. Could you tell us what you saw and heard going on at the time of the impact.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: At the time, the projectile hit the Bitas, I was at the New Sarajevo police station. Just before the impact, my colleagues and I had heard a sound that we had definitely never heard before throughout those years of war. It was like a huge droning sound passing through the town. A projectile always makes a sound when it impacts against something, but this was a sound that I was unfamiliar with, followed by a powerful explosion. I left the police station, perhaps three or four minutes after the explosion. Some of my mates had gone on. They had left the building to go and see if there were any victims that they could assist. All I saw at that time was a huge cloud of dust; and after that, I just went straight back to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: When did you actually begin investigations into the events at this location, at the Bitas building?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: On the 22nd of August, 1995, New Sarajevo municipality and especially the section around the Bitas building and Dolac-Malta was subjected to one of the most severe bouts of shelling. It was for our own safety that we couldn't carry out an on-site investigation at the Bitas building that same day. The police had been securing the scene throughout the night,; and then the next day on the 23rd of August, an on-site investigation team was put together, a forensic team. The day seemed more peaceful than the previous one, and there was an opportunity to have an on-site investigation which was therefore conducted the next day.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Did you make a photographic record of the scene?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I ask for ter number 00071 to be displayed, please; and then following that, I would like page 1 of ter 00071 and then page 2, please. And while we're waiting for this -- oh, we don't have to wait any time at all. If we could move on to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanefendic, do you recognise the documents in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is a photo file that I put together at the scene where the projectile impacted against the Bitas building on the 23rd of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, there's a photograph which appears in front of you on the right-hand side of the screen. Could you -- do you recognise this photograph? Tell us what it depicts.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: I do. This is the Bitas building. The photograph shows the Bitas building; the building that the projectile hit. This shows the south-western front of the building, which is exactly the side of the building hit by the projectile. The arrow that you can see in this photograph shows the exact point of impact of the projectile, which was between the second and third floors. Down on the ground, you can see the evidence of damage caused by the impact. I will use an arrow to mark the spot on the photograph. Perhaps two metres back from there --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Just a moment, please, Mr. Hasanefendic. We've -- we seem to have lost the image or it's been overmagnified. Thank you. We have the image in front of us. You were indicating that you wished to mark something?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes. I wanted to indicate with an arrow the spot which would be two metres further in where a person was killed by the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I have this photograph marked as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And perhaps I could note for the record that the arrow at the top of the photograph depicts what is the witness has described as the centre of the explosion, and the arrow at the bottom of the photograph indicates what the witness has described as the location at which someone was killed as a result.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be admitted as Exhibit P240, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you wish to continue on the same subject.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I was prepared to move to another paragraph. So if you have a question with respect to this photograph, I would respectfully suggest that the time would be opportune.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. For the same incident, do you want to continue on this since you -- perhaps you're going to ask the question I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I will continue with this incident. The questioning is not quite over with, Your Honours. If I could have page 9 of this same ter number, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: With respect to the top photo on page 9, Mr. Hasanefendic, do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: That photograph in my file that I made depicts the other side of the Bitas building, so that should be the north-east side. And it shows the damage on that side of the building caused by the explosion of that projectile.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: What does the arrow denote?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: The arrow shows the extensive damage on that side of the building caused by the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So just to reinforce what you said, then, the photograph which we've marked as P240 is what you have described as the impact side of this explosion, and you've just said this photograph is the other side?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Precisely. So I'm going to repeat. The previous photograph that we've seen shows the north-west side, the side of impact; and this one shows the other side, the back of the Bitas building showing the damage caused by the explosion of the projectile. Because it's extensive damage, and it was a large explosive device. It was a modified air bomb.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: I was just wanting to clarify your use of the word "other."

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I have this page marked as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Noting for the record, there are two photographs on this page. I would just propose to put the whole page in rather than split them up.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I could ask the witness in one question what the second photograph depicts, in fact.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: On this photograph, we see pieces of furniture and files because it was an office building, housing a company, and this debris was propelled out of the building by the explosion. This was found below the north-east side, the back that we've just seen on the other photograph. So due to the impact of the projectile, that -- there was a large explosive fusion that propelled material out of the building, so we see the debris of furniture and files on the concrete pavement.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So perhaps now we could have the page marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P241, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Did you recover any fragments of remains of the bomb, Mr. Hasanefendic?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. In the course of our investigation, we found parts of a metal projectile between 30 and 120 centimetres wide.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If I could just stop you for a moment, Mr. Hasanefendic.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I would ask, Mr. Registrar, to pull up page 23 of this same ter number, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you recognise that, Mr. Hasanefendic?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It's a photograph that I made on the spot on the 22nd of August, 1995, which gives a forensic scale for this photograph of pieces of the projectile that hit the building. Those are metal fragments from 30 to 120 centimetres wide. Those are fragments of the projectile that we found on the site of the Bitas bombing.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you make a report on the incident, Mr. Hasanefendic?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes. A comprehensive crime investigation and forensic report was made on this incident; my report, the photo file, and all the other records that we made based on the evidence found on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Before there picture is removed, perhaps I could ask that it be marked as the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P242, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And could I then ask, Mr. Registrar, for ter 186 at pages 2 and 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanefendic, do you recognise the document that appears in your language in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. That's my report on the first forensic investigation of the crime scene of the shelling of the Bitas building of 22nd August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I direct you on this page to the last sentence that appears on paragraph 4. Do you note there the direction from which the projectile that caused the explosion came?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was dated there that it was the determined on the spot that the said projectile had flown in from the aggressor's position in the south-west.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And who controlled the position?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me, madam Prosecutor. If I'm not mistaken the witness just answered your question of where the bomb came from by saying that it flew in from the aggressor's position in the south-west. Now what I read in the official report is that it came from was the south-east. Could you clarify, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, having drawn my attention to the official report, I can say this is an old translation and we had a subsequent revised translation prepared yesterday correcting this, and it obviously wasn't done in time and, with my apologies, to be uploaded on the system. But perhaps to put the issue to bed, we could ask the witness to read out the sentence in question and have the interpreters translate it.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanefendic, could you read what is set out in the last line in paragraph 4, please.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: It reads: "On the scene, it was determined that the said projectile -- device had flown in from the direction of the aggressor's position -- south-west."

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Hasanefendic, is this finding as to the origin of fire the team conclusion?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: It's definitely the conclusion of the entire team. But following our procedure, the final conclusion is the responsibility of the bomb squad's technician in this case, and he concluded just as we did that the projectile had flown in from the direction of the aggressor's position, to the south-west.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanefendic, are you aware what methods were used in this case to determine the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. At first, during our on-site investigation, our purpose was to find the centre of the explosion; then when we established on the basis of the damage that the centre of the explosion was between the second and third floors, inside the building, but no more than one metre away from the window close to the staircase, it was very easy for us to establish by our standard procedure, standard forensic procedure, where the projectile came from, and that was south-west.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Did you assist in making that determination?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I took part in our joint work, assisting the bomb squad technician, but the final conclusion was his. I detected the evidence, we determined the centre of the explosion together, and he made the final report and the conclusion on the direction of the origin of the projectile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Prosecutor, I believe I have a question to ask because the witness is saying that the projectile came from the south-west, is that right, from the south-west? When we look at photograph P240, we saw that the point of impact was on the north-west side of the building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that is the south-west, the side of that building; and even today, that building still looks like it used to during the war. It's the south-west facade, so the first photograph that we saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite right. You said that you "assisted in -- in the determination of the origin of the projectile, together with a bomb squad technician," and you said, "the projectile came from the south-west," I quote; and "from the," and I quote the again, the aggressor's positions. But several times here, we've been shown the line of confrontation as it was in Sarajevo at the time; and if memory serves me right, both armies were always facing each other. Therefore, this south-west direction you mentioned was a direction where we -- where both armies were to be found. Therefore, this bomb squad technician, how was he in a position to say that the projectile was coming from the so-called aggressor? Do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I certainly understand your question. But, first of all, our job on the spot was to determine and to analyse the whole situation on the scene, like in this case. So our first task was to find the centre of the explosion and we did that. Let me repeat again. The technician from the bomb squad is a person who is involved in the investigation team, and his job is to determine the direction of fire. I remember that when we worked on this investigation, we all came to a joint conclusion that the projectile had definitely flown in from south-west. But let me repeat, the one who makes the final conclusion and the final report is the technician from the bomb squad. Another thing that happened during that investigation is that two persons approached us - I don't remember their names, but the police inspector probably took down their details - and these two persons stated they had even seen the projectile fly in from the south-west. They saw it while it was in the air. It was our first encounter with a device of this kind, this modified air bomb. But by studying it later, we found that the statements of the witnesses were quite probable, because it flies in more slowly and its primary aim is not impact. Its primary purpose is massive destruction and intimidation, and that is reflected in the official report and conclusion that we made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Two questions. You say the final conclusion, as to the direction from which the bomb came, is the job of the bomb squad technician. Is there a report from him, from that person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] His report must be in existence because our police procedure envisages that once we complete the on-site investigation, each member of the investigation team makes their own report, just as I make a forensic report complete with a photo file, sketch, and a request for expertise. The investigating judge makes his own report, the police inspector takes witness statements, and of course the bomb squad technician has to make his own report to make this case official. So I'm sure his report exists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I must ask, Ms. Edgerton, are we hearing from the bomb squad technician.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: In respect of this specific incidents, Your Honours, it's not our intention that you hear from the bomb squad technician; however, it is our intention that you hear from the man who served at the relevant time as the chief of the forensic department; in other words, the supervisor of the bomb squad technicians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But what we're being told is that it is the bomb squad technician who ultimately determines the direction from which the bomb came. So his determination is conclusive, am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right. His conclusion official and final.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The next question is you spoke of your team using the standard procedure for determining the direction from which the bomb came, and what is this "standard procedure"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this case, our primary purpose was to find the centre of the explosion. We found it easy to determine the centre of the explosion due to extensive damage done to the building and based on the concentration of that damage between the second and third floors. After that, the bomb squad technician sets a compass at the centre of the explosion and very easily, based on the traces of the explosion and the juxtaposition of the explosion, determines the direction of fire. With mortar shells, it's much easier to establish that direction than with modified projectiles such as this one. But precisely for that reason, we spent a lot of time working on this investigation in order to achieve absolute certainty that the direction of fire was indeed south-west, as we finally agreed. So the greatest amount of time in that investigation was spent on determining the centre of the explosion because it was a very large explosion, the kind of which we had never encountered before. And we spent a lot of care and time trying to determine its exact centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: At first, he determines the centre of the explosion, and you say that was -- that was done. After determining the centre of the explosion, the bomb squad technician then employs his compass; and, as you say, he very easily, based on the traces of the explosion and the juxtaposition of the explosion, determines the direction of the fire.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. Correct. So relative to the centre of the explosion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's the sciences that underlies this that I would like to have explained. You say it was a conclusion arrived at very easily, but I would be helped by having an explanation of the science that is the basis of this conclusion. The next question I would like to ask is: In this case, was the determination made that the bomb came from the direction of the south-west, or was it also determined that it came not only from the south-west but from the aggressor's position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this case, it was established that the projectile came from south-west, from the aggressor's positions. We determined that based on the procedure that I have described to you and based on -- but mostly based on the procedure that I have described to you. That's it. But that is an official report written by the bomb squad technician that I have mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And that determination was also made very easily, I presume?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Notwithstanding the fact that, as Judge Mindua said, both warring factions were relatively near to each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is true. I don't know, in fact, whether they were relatively close to that area, because I have never been there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You can't help us, then, with the distance between the warring factions in that particular area in the south-west?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot tell you what the distance between the warring factions was in that particular area, because I've never been there. But in that specific case that we investigated, I can tell you this: After we established where the projectile impacted and calculated the height of the building and took witness statements, witnesses who told us that the projectile fell -- witnesses who told us that they had seen the projectile in the air, not even close to the building, but back in the area called Cengic Vila, based on that all that, we determined that the projectile from come Serb positions in the south-west. After that, the projectile fragments were submitted to expertise, and we received a report on that projectile and similar projectiles, that we called modified air bombs, that had fallen on Sarajevo. And as far as I know, most of them had arrived from that direction. And on that basis, I wrote this sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In order to make your determination, not only as to the direction from which the bomb came but that it came from the aggressor's position, would you also not to have taken into account the -- the position of the -- of the other army, the ABiH army, in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, we took into account the position of the BiH army, but this time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I put that you are not able to tell us about the distance between the two armies in that area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, I'm saying this again, concerning this specific case. My job was to collect all the evidence on the spot, including the metal fragments of that projectile. I am not the person who has the task to make such a analyses on the scene and to consider the distance between the BiH army and the Serb army. My job on the spot was to collect and preserve the evidence, in this case involving the impact of a modified air bomb. The person who takes such factors into account, including the it distance between the two armies, is the bomb squad representative. So I am in no way able to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So the bomb squad technician is the man. Let us adjourn for 20 minutes. May I invite you to take your seats. I'm being told that we have a special schedule for the various breaks for Friday, and the legal officer is going to pass me the schedule. I was following the tradition schedule. We'll go to 12.30 when we will take a one-hour lunch break, so we still have another ten, 12 minutes. Ms. Edgerton, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If I may deal with a couple of matters relating to the last document which was on the screen, which I didn't tender, ter number 186 at pages 2 and 3. Somebody has a mobile phone ringing. Could I have that document up on the screen again, please. And I should note for Your Honours, the translation which appeared on the left-hand side of the screen which caused some confusion for all of us was, in fact, not the translation for that document at all. And as I said earlier, I will undertake to have the translation available before the end of court today. This document is the one which the witness commended extensively about, and at this moment if I could have that enter as the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P243, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I go back then -- and this is not the translation that appears on the left-hand side of this page is not the translation for this document. It's the translation for a completely different document. Thank you. If I could go to the same ter number, 186, at pages 4 and 5, I would appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanefendic, could you tell us what the document is that appears on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: This is an Official Note by a crime officer of Novo Sarajevo as a result of the on-site investigation on the attack on the Bitas building on the 22nd of August, 1995, and the note was made on the 25th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Was this crime investigations officer a member of your team? And if we could scroll down through the document, please.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was. He was a member of my team. You see his name under number 2. At the time, he was the duty crime forensic officer from the Novo Sarajevo police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, just at the very bottom of my screen with the paragraph -- in the paragraph that begins in your language with the word, "modifikovana". Could you tell us whether or not this report sets out information as to the origin of fire.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: It reads that the origin of fire was the south-western side and that is the aggressor's position at Orahovac. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: To your knowledge, is your own document as to the origin of fire and the conclusion in this document as to origin of fire consistent with what was contained in the ballistics report on this investigation, as to origin of fire?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter correction: That was not Orahovac, is what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes. In my report and my colleague's report, it is stated that the projectile came from the south-westerly direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If we could just go up a little bit in the report, to see the personalities involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, I see a name at number 4, Mr. Hasanefendic: Mirsad Dzelilovic. Could you explain to us who he was.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: The gentleman was a colleague of mine, Mirsad Dzelilovic. He was the bomb squad technician from the Security Services Centre in Sarajevo, and he worked together with us on this investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If I could have this entered as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P244, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanefendic, now, with respect to this exhibit and the previous exhibit, did you, in the course of your work as a forensic technician with the Novo Sarajevo municipality, ever come upon a situation where conclusions as to origin of fire made by your team differed from those made by the bomb squad technicians?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: We always worked on these investigations concerning shell impacts or other artillery impacts together, and we never, ever, not even once, reached differing conclusions as to the origin of fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, if I could just go to the next page of this document, that would be page 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanefendic, you mentioned two witnesses, who later - if you could go down the page - who later it came to light that corroborated these findings as to origin of fire; do you see their names here?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I see their names.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And what are they, please.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Abdulah Cancar and Zada Borovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Were statements taken from those two individuals, to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: I don't recall that. I do remember that a man and a woman approached us as we were investigating the scene and gave us their statements that they saw the incident. There was a colleague of ours, an officer, who noted down the information that they provided. I don't know whether actually he took their official statements, because he is the person charged with taking statements from eye-witnesses --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: -- whereas, I work with the collection of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Moving to a ter number that we dealt with previously, 00071, at page number 24.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you see the picture in front of you, Mr. Hasanefendic, on the screen? Do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is the photograph I made showing the direction from which the projectile flew in, but I have to note that in normal times this photograph should have been focussed at least ten centimetres more to the right. Why? Because this was -- the point at which I stood when I was talking the photograph was the last boundary where I could stand in order not to expose myself to enemy fire, but otherwise I should have, in fact, taken the photograph from a slightly different angle.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And on the compass, which direction is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: This should be the direction to the south-west; however, as we are looking at it now, it should show a bit more to the right. It is south-west, but further to the right would have been more accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I have this photograph marked as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P245, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: According to special schedule for today, Your Honours, it looks like I may have run out of time. I'm in Your Honours's hands. There would be, maximum, seven to ten minutes worth of questions after this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I think it would be neater if you just finish.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanefendic, do you recall on 22nd of August at the time that you heard the noise you described in your testimony and the detonation, do you recall any military activity in the area other than the shelling which prevented you from going out to investigate the explosion?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, there was no military activity in the area we were at the time. There was shelling throughout the day, though, but I do not recall any military activity in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing any active Bosnian forces in the area at the time?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: I did not observe any active Bosnian army troops at the time and in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Were there any mortars that you recall in that area?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: I remember that I had never seen a single mortar in that area in -- in my life. Well, I speak for myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: In -- do you have any knowledge or any experience of shells or explosives of similar size and calibre to what was used in this incident being used or in the possession of the Bosnian military forces?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: I have no information about the explosive devices of this sort ever having been in possession of the Bosnian forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'd like to deal with two photographs, please, before I conclude. One which we've seen before; that's 2956. That's the satellite image. And, Mr. Registrar, the next photograph after that will be 2495.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can you on this photograph, Mr. Hasanefendic, mark the location of the incident we've been discussing for the last wile on 22nd August 1995, please.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can mark the building accurately. This is Hrasnica, Electroprivida, and this is where the building is.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... marking -- we may be in a situation where we might need to do this again, but at the moment let's move forward. Marking the Bitas building with a circle, now with an arrow can you indicate what you recall was determined as the direction of fire, please.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: It would perhaps be better if the image could be zoomed in on. But at any rate, this is the direction of fire. As the image is quite small, I will just draw a small arrow. This is the direction of fire. A higher resolution, however, would be more helpful. I could draw it in more detail.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Perhaps to close this issue, Your Honours, we could have this marked as an exhibit, but it may assist everyone more if I have the witness mark on the same photograph which has been delivered to the parties recently. It's a higher resolution and covers a greater why area than what we see on the screen in front of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Could I just ask the witness if your latest indication is correct, it would seem to me that the direction of fire is from the east, is that correct, from the east? You have a north arrow in the top corner of the picture which enables you to identify the -- the directions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. That's why I said that I can barely make out the different quarters of town on this map. But if this is at northern side, the top -- that's why I asked for a higher resolution image because I can get my bearings there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in my cross-examination, I was intending to put the question His Honour Judge Harhoff just put. I don't want him to have this erased. I want this mark to remain where it is, because he first drew this line; and when this is tendered into evidence, if it is going to tendered, I don't want it to be deleted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I, as a witness, would like to say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, what are you saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This arrow here, I've only just noticed that this is the main street. Can I draw what I want on the image? The resolution is really poor, and I am doing my best to concentrate and see which part of town this is. The arrow should, in fact, point a bit more down to the south-west. I just realise this is the Zmaja od Bosne Street. If you want to, you can keep the first arrow, but this is, in fact, what the arrow should point to, in relation to the Bitas building, and that is roughly that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Can you then clarify, at least for me, whether your arrow that you have now drawn indicates the direction of the mortar or the direction towards the area from which the mortar was shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I just ask you -- you were saying where the arrow is -- you were actually referring to this area at the top, pointing to the north; is that right? Are you talking in relation to that? Because I really don't know the size of the world on this map to know what you're referring to when you say north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me, Witness. I should have clarified this. As I understand the picture in front of us, north is the top. If you look at the top left corner of the picture, you will see a small arrow indicating the north. Now, my question is you have identified Bits the building, and you have put an arrow pointing down towards the lower left side of the picture. And you have put an are arrow there; you have marked that. And the question is quite simple: Is the direction -- the arrow is your -- is your arrow pointing down towards the point from which the mortar was fired, or does your arrow indicate the direction of the mortar when it came in and hit the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The arrow I drew shows the direction from which it flew in, if we're talking about the Bitas building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You are referring to what's presently the second lower arrow on the photograph in front of you; is that correct, Mr. Hasanefendic?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's the arrow that I was intending to draw, but the poor resolution made it impossible for me to get my bearings and see the streets that are depicted here. You can erase the top arrow, as far as I'm concerned. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes, that would be fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And I should note, perhaps some of the confusion was caused by the imprecision in my initial question, which only referred to direction of fire, and that in translation can easily cause a misunderstanding. Could we erase the top arrow, please, which the witness indicated was drawn in error, due also in part to the lack of clarity of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I asked for the Chamber to rule on this; and in the mean time, the arrow has already been deleted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, the Chamber will consider whether it should be replaced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The arrow is to be replaced. The Chamber has heard the evidence of the witness. It's for the Chamber to make what we will of the evidence, in light of the explanation that he has given. But the arrow is to be replaced. Please draw and replace the first arrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Due to the image itself, I made roughly this arrow, but this isn't part of my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regardless of both of these arrows --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Very briefly at this point, then, Mr. Hasanefendic, from which direction did the bomb come from? The top arrow on this photograph or the bottom arrow?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: The on-site investigation established that the direction of fire was in fact as depicted by the bottom arrow showing towards the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, you're facing a technological problem. We only have five minutes of tape [Realtime transcript missing words "of tape"] left.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I can speak very quickly Your Honours. If I could have this be marked as the next exhibit. I will ask then for one final photograph, 2495.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P245, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If we could now have 2495 [sic] on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why can't the transcript reflect what I said. I said, "we only have five minutes of tape left."

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Sorry. 2945. I'm loosing time on the tape because of my own difficulties with mathematics. 2945. No. It's coming?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, I commend you for the efforts that you have made.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Defeated by technology, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will take the break now for one hour. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.48 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'll just deal with two matters. On February the 9th, the Prosecution filed a motion for the admission of written statements, pursuant to Rule 92 ter in respect of four witnesses. Now, the Defence response is expected on Friday, the 23rd of February. I believe that means that the Defence has until that date to respond. One of the witnesses mentioned in the motion is scheduled to testify on Thursday, the 22nd of February, that is W-91; and in that regard, it would be helpful if we could decide this motion on Monday, the 19th, and so I am inquiring of the Defence whether they could provide a response earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. So we'll probably take the same line, and we'll go along with your decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, on the 1st ever February, the Prosecution filed a motion for the admission of four written statements, pursuant to Rule 92 ter, and the motion pertains to two statements of witness W-12 and two statements of witness Suljevic. The Defence did not respond to the motion. The Trial Chamber grants the Prosecution motion and admits the four statements into evidence upon fulfilment of the conditions set out in the Rule. Please bring the witness in, and, Ms. Edgerton, to conclude her examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It's now afternoon, Mr. Hasanefendic. To conclude your testimony today, I'd like you to deal with, again, some further images on the screen in front of you, the first two of which you see now. Do you recognise these two images; one on the right and one on the left?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Sorry. Before you answer, could you tell us what they are.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: These two photographs depict the front and back of the Bitas building that was hit by this modified air bomb.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: All right. For the record, the photograph on the left-hand side of the screen bears the number P2495 [sic]; and the one on the right side of the screen bears the number - I've done it again, Your Honours - bears the number 2945; and the one on the right-hand side of the screen, bears the number 2944.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, looking at number 2945, when you say that this is the front side of the Bitas building, what direction does this side face?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: This is the front facade of the Bitas building, which faces south-west.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Does this then depict the impact site of the bomb that you investigated on August 22nd, 1995?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes. On that side of the building, we can see the point of impact of that air bomb.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And going to the one the right-hand side of your screen, 2944, does this photograph depict what you described as the back-- the exit side of the bomb.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: That shows precisely the back of the building and the damage caused by the explosion of the air bomb.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, do these two photographs resemble in any way the Bitas building in Sarajevo as it appears today in 2007?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: This building has not been renovated so far, not until the day when I travelled to this Tribunal, and it looks exactly the same as it did in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: The damage is the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If we could have up on the screen, please P -- Prosecution Exhibit 245, one further time. The ter number -- I don't need the ter number now that it's got an exhibit number, because I had a look at the transcript over the break and I -- apologies, I have to look at -- what I'd like on the screen, please, Mr. Registrar, is the image of the map that the witness last marked with the two arrows, so that's probably 246 then. It originally bore the ter 2956, but I was looking for the one that he -- thank you. Over the break, I had a look at the transcript and, I realised that the transcript lacks some clarity as to the description or the meaning of what was intended by the lower arrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: With that in mind, I would like to ask, Mr. Hasanefendic, this lower arrow of the two, that appears on the photograph that is on the screen in front of you, does it point to where the bomb was fired from, or does it point to where the bomb was flying to? Is that clear, Mr. Hasanefendic?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: It's clear. That's the direction determined on the spot by the bomb squad technician, this lower arrow. I made a mistake because it's image was not ideal.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Hasanefendic, that wasn't the question I asked you. I asked you if the arrow pointed to where the bomb was fired from or in the direction the bomb was flying to.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: The arrow shows, as we've say, the direction from which the projectile flew in. That's the only thing we know based on that investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I am going to leave it at that, Your Honour, and that concludes my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I note you spent about two hours, twice the time which you had estimated for examination-in-chief and cross-examination. Earlier next week, the Chamber will be issuing a note, setting out the time spent by the Prosecution so far. Mr. Tapuskovic, cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I omitted to tender the photographs, 2944 and 2945, the numbers which I got correct for the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We will admit that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, we admit 02945 as Exhibit P247, and 02944 as Exhibit P248.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you give me the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would kindly ask that this photograph, 245, remain on the screen, so that I don't have to recall it later. Could the witness point out -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I appear here for General Dragomir Milosevic. My name is Branislav Tapuskovic, Attorney-at-law. Can you show me where Cengic Vila is on this photo?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: First of all, I cannot show you here where Cengic Vila is here, because there are two locations by the same name. Cengic Vila 1 and Cengic Vila 2. Cengic Vila, if we look at this Bitas building, goes all along the street that leads to the radio and television, and on the right-hand side is Cengic Vila 1. If we look towards the radio television building --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Towards the north?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: No, no. It faces west. But there is also Cengic Vila 2. Do you want me to point out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Just tell me first about the one that faces west.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: So if we look from this perspective --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... colour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please use a pen with a different colour, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So looking from this perspective, Cengic Vila is located, number 1, just as this upper arrow that I already marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Show.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: I'm indicating. That is Cengic Vila 1 and Cengic Vila 2 is in this direction, on the border between Otok neighbourhood and Hrasna neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke about two eye-witnesses who said -- in fact, you say that they said the projectile had come from Cengic Vila direction?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: That's not what I said. What I said is this: Two witnesses approached us and said that going through Cengic Vila neighbourhood, they saw the projectile in the air, and it was moving at such a speed that it was clearly visible. They didn't say it came from Cengic Vila; they said that they were at the time in Cengic Vila neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What did they say about the direction? Where did it come from?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: They didn't say that. They only said they saw it above Cengic Vila. That's what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you speak to them?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: I did not speak to them. The crime inspector -- crime police inspector spoke to them. I didn't even remember their names until I read them here. But their reports were also an indicator of the direction from which the projectile had come from, and it meant something to the bomb squad technician.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Because that could be a very important testimony. How come the police inspector didn't ask these people where the bomb was coming from? And that would have solved the problem. We wouldn't have to bother --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't see how he can answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But can you answer this. Document DD00-0759 is this witness' statement of March 1997, 10th March 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it please be shown to Mr. Hasanefendic. DD00-0759.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is that your statement?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I still don't see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is this your statement?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: I see my name here, my father's name, but I would also like to see the actual text.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Look at the end of the document, it's page 3.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: That is my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Does this passage relate precisely to this incident of the 22nd of August 1995. I could take you back to it, but I wanted to save some time.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does relate to that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on the last page as well in English, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The investigator asked you: "How did you determine that the fire came from south-west?" Answer: "The direction of the incoming fire was determined by the ballistics expert, and I was present when he came to that conclusion. I would like to say that as a scene of crime officer, it was my duty to preserve evidence." Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph we read, "We determined the direction from which the projectile was fired based on to the damage onto the building." So is it correct that you determined the direction based on damage caused to the building?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: You have to understand one thing. Is not I who determined the direction. That job was done by the bomb squad technician. My job on the scene was to collect evidence, such as parts of the projectile; to preserve that evidence; to make a sketch of the scene; to prepare a photographic file; bag all the evidence and send it to expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now focus on the rest of this text. "The impact was visible on the south-west side of the building. In fact, it would have been better to state the direction as south because the projectile came more from south, from south rather than south-west. It would have been better if we had stated the direction as south because the projectile had come from south rather than south-west."

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: It's very -- I can explain it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can we also draw that line as well on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Maybe I answer this question, please? Will you allow me? When we did that on-site investigation, of course, we followed the entire procedure that I described earlier. However, forensic techniques and bomb squad techniques and all the people who attended the scene, at that moment, may always take a broader area to describe the direction of fire. We couldn't go to the spot to confirm and we were not able to see -- as the Honourable Judge asked me, we couldn't see the spot where from where it was fired. But it is a standard normal procedure of forensic technique to take an area as a possible source of fire, and that's why we made the description worded as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I heard a number of your answers so far. Let me remind you that in the first attempt to explain this on the 10th of March, 1997, you responded to the very explicit question of the investigator by saying, "It would have been better to state south as the direction of fire, because the projectile came from the south rather than south-west."

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: When I made that statement, I reviewed my photo file as well. But to explain what I said, I said that because the photograph showed more precisely the direction where the projectile came from, but I took a broader area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't want to argue with this witness, but I just want him to draw that line as well on that map, 245.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What line is it that you want him to draw? What line?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Relative to that building, I want him to draw a line that would indicate the direction showing that the projectile came from south as he believed then in 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that has not been his evidence today. That may have been what he had written in miss original report. He indicated that prior to making the statement, he had an opportunity to review the investigative file and the related documentation and to look at his photographs again. He made that correction. My submission, Your Honours, would be if he were draw to another arrow indicating south as the direction of the fire, he is asked to -- he is being asked to create evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. It's for the Chamber to assess. Draw the line depicting the bomb coming from the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right. I just want him to show graphically what he said the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have instructed him to do it, Mr. Tapuskovic. Did you understand that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But he doesn't have the picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, let the relevant map be put on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, I want the map from before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What's the number? Ms. Edgerton, can you help us with this? P246.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 245, not 246, as I said a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And am I supposed now to draw a line going to the south?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: No, what you said in 1997. Draw the line that goes to -- that goes south as you said then, and the Trial Chamber will decide?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: I am telling you, again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Listen to me. You will do what I tell you to do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. All right. If I have to draw a line southward, that would be it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, speaking of this event in this building, I have to ask you, do you have medical records to accompany all this that you have been telling us? Do you have medical records describing the injuries of people who were, according to you, injured on that spot?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: I don't have those medical records. In our case, it was collected by the crime police inspector from the Security Services Centre of Sarajevo. The forensics department does not collect medical documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how we can make any conclusions at all about this if the medical documentation is missing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's a comment which is not appropriate. You're not allowed to make comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I put it to you that the medical documentation exists but you deliberately did not put it in this file?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: I really have to tell you, again. As a scene of crime officer, it is not my job to collect medical documentation. My job is to make my own report, the photo file, the sketch. So I really have knowing to do with it. This is the job of a scene of crime officer in the field.
