The police were wearing uniforms at the time throughout the city. They would normally carry a pistol and an automatic rifle, a Heckler Koch or perhaps a Kalashnikov, depending. As to the Bosna unit --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: We need a few minutes because I have to wait until transcript and translation catch up, but I question the foundation in this case, because where I would submit -- how would the witness be in a position to answer what weapons the Bosna unit has had or has, had at the time, when he's given no evidence about the Bosna unit. Perhaps the question could be rephrased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, I think he can answer that. I think he can answer it from his experience.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll answer. As to the Bosna unit, I was in no sort of contact with the special unit named Bosna, nor did I know at the time what sort of weapons they were carrying. All I was saying was in relation to the Novo Sarajevo police station because that was my personal experience. So much from me as concerns the Bosna unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But that unit, the Bosna unit, that's what it was called, wasn't it? This was a special unit of the MUP, the best-trained unit, the best-trained police unit, was it not?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: That is quite right. That's why there were called special MUP units. It was nicknamed the Bosna unit. It was put together after the Serb specialists and the first -- the Muslim and Croat specialists parted ways at the outbreak of the war itself. What sort of weapons did they have? I don't know. I was not a member. I can't say. I really don't know. I never even worked with those people throughout the war. No sort of police business at all was shared.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So those were police units, police forces, of the former country which became a part of the BH MUP later on, right?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: This unit was always a special unit of the then-socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in the former country. These people were police officers. They were always members of this unit and they continued to be just that in the war. They were special police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In that case, I have one document for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please preserve the map first, the map as it has been marked, as a Defence exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll exhibit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, unfortunately, we cannot exhibit it because another document was published before we were able to capture the image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, as it has been explained to me by those who have more learning in this matter, the document was on the screen, you used it, but you never asked for it to be admitted, so the officer removed it from the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I understand it was your own case manager who put on the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would be willing to drop all of my remaining questions if only the witness could please have that map again and mark what he has already marked before. If we can be granted time for that particular exercise, I would, in exchange, give up all of my further questioning. For me, as Defence counsel, that map is exceptionally important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not proceeding on the basis of exchanges. If you have proper questions to ask, the Court will allow that, and if it is proper to have this replaced, then we'll do it. Let us have it replaced and re-marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: As we deal with that, Your Honour, I do recall I was cautioned earlier on today by Your Honours as to the time I had used. I was told it was two hours. I'm not sure whether or not that calculation included Your Honours' questions and other objections, or it was -- it didn't include that. But I'm also just noticing the time for this cross-examination, unless I'm mistaken in my calculation, is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's just about the same time that you used, yes. There's nothing wrong with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No. I'm simply noting the time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There is a technical explanation to be given and I think the court deputy is in a much better position than I am to offer it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. I spoke with the technician in the AV booth who did broadcast the image that was marked by the witness, and because that image was broadcast, captured on the tape, we can extract that from the videotape and have it uploaded into the system. However, it won't be quite as clear, but it will be still be legible. That's the explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Therefore, we can mark it as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D70, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. Tapuskovic, do you have more questions that are relevant and pointed?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have two matters to raise. Firstly, this document, D000-0757 -- that's the one, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you see that? The document produced by the 12th Division. The date is the 28th of March.

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Of course I see it, but I do not realise what this has to do with my job. Can you please explain? Would you be so kind? A SOCer, scene of crime officer, what do I have to do with maps denoting all the positions of the army of Republika Srpska? The Fikret Prevljak Brigade or any of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's not for you to ask questions. If the questions are improper, the Chamber will rule them so.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I'm somewhat confused. The document I have, DD00-0757, is dated the 28th of March, 1995, and I just need some clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is the date of this one?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I don't see any date noted on the transcript. That's why I would like to be sure we're all referring to the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's right there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The one on the screen is marked the 28th of March, 1995. That coincides with what you have. Let's proceed, quickly. It's now 16 minutes to 5.00. Count-down.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you say you never laid eyes on any serious weapons in Sarajevo. That's why I'm asking. You didn't, did you?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I never saw a serious weapon throughout the war there, at least not in my area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is it -- do you mean heavy weapons or is it "serious"?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mortars, mortars is what I mean. There you go. A straightforward question. Mortars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mortars then, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never saw a single mortar throughout the war, that is, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This is from the command of the 12th Division which covered central Sarajevo, Commander Prevljak, about weapons being reassigned to a different unit. It's an order, right? Can you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: It says "Fikret Prevljak, Commander." Now please listen. "I hereby order: Reassign 82-millimetre mortars from NSB 3 to the Bosna unit of the MUP." This is a serious weapon, you will agree, won't you, which is hereby being assigned to the MUP, to one of its units. Did you at least see this one serious weapon in your area? I suppose not all of your investigations were about sniping, were they?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Again, I never saw a single heavy weapon throughout the war in the areas in which I spent time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have this exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can we find out the difference between serious and heavy weapons? The subject is coming up again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We had it before, "serious," and I suspected that what was meant was "heavy," "heavy weapon." What is the term that you use in B/C/S? Could you use it so that we have a proper interpretation of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, to my mind, this mortar that we had been discussing and the mortar that we will be discussing for the most part of this trial, I mean it's an exceptionally heavy. To my mind, a mortar is an exceptionally serious weapon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me, then, that you have variously used "serious" and "heavy." Continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think you are right, I have been using the two. But even a pistol is a heavy weapon to my mind. Even pistol can kill a human being. What I would like to do now is to tender this as a Defence exhibit, the document we've just used. If the Chamber could please admit the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The witness did not confirm anything in relation to it. So in accordance with the rules that we apply, it will not be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not even marked for identification, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be marked for identification as D71.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: One more question, Mr. Tapuskovic. I think I have been very lenient with you. Just one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] DD00-0768. This is this witness's statement dated the 16th of May, 2006. Just a very brief paragraph from that statement. Second page. That paragraph. It begins with the word "Snipers ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, does it read -- first of all, is this your statement?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: It reads: "Snipers shooting at the city would not stay in one fixed position. The Bosnian army also had snipers." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SANJIN HASANEFENDIC
utterances.text: I personally never saw a single one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Anti-snipers. Just correct that. In the English version, it's anti-snipers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I meant. It has obviously been translated in a slightly different way that I --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, to understand this, one needs to read the whole paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is the question which you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the question was: "Did the Bosnian army, and primarily the MUP, have sniper weapons."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you in a position to say whether the Bosnian army and primarily the MUP have sniper weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot say that. The statement, and this sentence here, were taken out of context. I never said that, because I have never seen anything like it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Never mind the statement. What is the answer to the question that I have asked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the answer to that question is that I cannot provide any information about whether it's Bosnian army had snipers because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If the Bosnian army also had anti-snipers, what weapons would those anti-snipers use?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, and I must say that happened very rarely because Serb snipers worked in a very coordinated way as we were able to see from our on-site investigation, the weapons that the Bosnian army could use against Serb snipers if they observed any were automatic or semi-automatic weapons. I never saw a single sniper, and I suppose they used automatic weapons for counter-snipers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We must conclude the cross-examination now, and is there any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: None? Okay. Then, Mr. Hasanefendic, that concludes your testimony. Thank you for giving it, and you may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And, in fact, the Chamber will adjourn the hearing until Monday at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 19th day of February, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.54 p.m.,
